contact_edits.before: The Russian Play is a scintillating exercise in style (owing more to Chekhov's short stories than his plays, whatever the script says) which also manages to be a moving meditation on poverty, oppression and love. I have now seen Michelle Monteith's performance as Sonya three times, and I can't say that it has improved; it was perfect the first time and it still is, impossibly mature, both technically and emotionally, in its instant switches from sardonic narrator to trusting heroine and back again. That the two women are in fact one is only revealed at the end, though I can't see any point in keeping that secret. As before, Monteith gets strong support from Shawn Campbell and Aaron Willis as the two (married) men in her life, which is more than you can say of Sonya herself; one, a poor gravedigger, breaks her heart, the other, a rich factory-owner, breaks her body. Also as before, and also invaluable in their contributions to matters of atmosphere and tension, are Tom Howell's violin-playing and Kimberly Purtell's cruelly acute lighting. The play's scale, and its key, may be minor but the overall achievement, under Natasha Mytnowych's direction, is major. - The Russian Play/ Essay runs until Feb. 17. Call 416-504-9971 for more information.
